segments.text: [Fictional demonstration visit; all participants are fictional.] Good morning. What brings you in today?
I have had a cough for four days. It keeps waking me up, and I am supposed to be back at work tomorrow. I thought I had better get it checked. I brought my medicine list too.
Thanks, let me take a look at that. Have you had any fever since the cough started?
No fever. I checked a couple of times at home because I wondered about that too.
And how has your health been otherwise? Any ongoing conditions I should know about?
I have asthma. I used to go to the clinic across town, but this office is much easier to get to from work.
My father has diabetes. He has been telling me I should find a regular doctor instead of just coming in when I am sick.
It is helpful to know about your family too. What medicines are you taking at the moment?
I still use albuterol. I brought the inhaler with me because I can never remember everything on the label. Here it is.
Thank you, that helps. Before we talk about treatment, have you ever had a reaction to a medicine?
I am allergic to sulfa; it gave me a rash years ago. I cannot remember the name on the bottle, but I remember the rash. It was miserable.
Do you have an allergy to penicillin as well?
I am not allergic to penicillin. I have taken that before without any trouble.
All right. Rest your arm here while I check your blood pressure. Then I will listen to your chest.
Your blood pressure is 126 over 78. You can relax your arm now.
Your heart rate is 84 beats per minute. Take a few slow breaths for me.
Okay. The coughing is mostly what is bothering me. I just want to get some sleep.
I think this is acute bronchitis. That would explain the cough. It can take a while to settle down, even when you are starting to feel better.
I do not think this is pneumonia. If things get worse, please call us so we can check you again.
Would an antibiotic help? I was hoping there might be something I could take.
We could try amoxicillin, but I don't think you need an antibiotic. I would leave that for now.
Start acetaminophen 500 milligrams by mouth every eight hours as needed. Let me write that down so you have the instructions at home.
Thanks. I was worried I would forget what we talked about as soon as I walked out.
You are welcome. Check with the front desk about a follow-up before you leave, and call if you have questions. [End of fictional demonstration.]
